source.citation: Aggregated peak tan δ values from Jones, D.I.G. 'Handbook of Viscoelastic Vibration Damping' (Wiley 2001) and Nashif, Jones, Henderson 'Vibration Damping' (Wiley 1985), cross-referenced against vendor datasheets (3M, EAR, Sorbothane). All values are widely cited reference points for the substrate-class, not original measurements.
source.data_origin: Published peak loss tangent at the material's design operating point. Each instance characterized by a single (T, f) sweet-spot value; full T×f surface is substrate-conditional and beyond the scope of this characterization.
source.ingestion_notes: Loss tangent η = tan δ = E''/E'. Quality factor at resonance: Q = 1/η = 1/tan δ. Damping ratio: ζ = η/2 = tan δ / 2. Critical damping (s-boundary) at tan δ = 2.0.

substrate_class_variant: polymeric material characterized by frequency- and temperature-dependent loss tangent tan δ; substrate-zero-analog for the F-001-conversion form is the conversion of mechanical vibration energy to heat
substrate_class_notes: F-001 chit_max bound does NOT apply directly to dissipative materials. F-001 form chit_max ≈ -ln(1 - η_conversion) requires drive and useful-work to be in DIFFERENT modes (electrical → mechanical for actuators, fuel → brake-power for engines, electrical → acoustic for loudspeakers). For damping materials, dissipation IS the useful work — there is no separate 'useful output' mode. F-001 chit_max → ∞ in the limit, which is the formula breaking down. The substrate-class scope of F-001 is: substrates with input/output mode-separation. Damping materials are *outside* that scope and instead test F-003 (regime structure from Q) directly.

substrate_class_statistics.design_pressure_summary: Industrial damping materials cluster Q in [0.5, 1.5] — the substrate-class fingerprint is engineering tuning of polymer formulation to land the operating point near the s-boundary. Three of eight characterized instances land at Q ≤ 0.67 (within 0.17 of critical), and one lands at Q = 0.5 exactly by design.
